summary: Gunwaith holds its clans together, keeps or breaks the Truce of the Grey Ford, leads the Ford Council and answers the great question of the sea: cross for the old claims, keep to the western shore, or sail to Aenor's relief.

weary_clans.name: Fifty Years of War
weary_clans.desc: Half a century of raid and reprisal has left every clan with a dead son and a grudge. The clans want to fight less, and cannot quite say why.

clan_halls_spirit.name: The Clan Halls
clan_halls_spirit.desc: The chiefs sit at the king's table and the king sits at theirs.

clans_as_one_spirit.name: The Clans as One
clans_as_one_spirit.desc: Hands joined across the king's cup: the clans have made one kingdom.

kings_peace.name: The King's Peace
kings_peace.desc: No raid, no reprisal, no blood-price in the king's name. The truce grows firmer each month it is kept.

war_thanes.name: The War-Thanes
war_thanes.desc: The thanes ride where they please and the king has promised to understand. Every month wears the truce thinner.

clan_levies.name: The Clan Levies
clan_levies.desc: Each clan owes a levy and has written the number on a roll.

highland_studs_spirit.name: The Highland Studs
highland_studs_spirit.desc: Hardy ponies bred on heather need little fodder, and carry their burdens over any moor.

war_chest.name: The War Chest of the West
war_chest.desc: The king's vaults are full, and the goods that might have gone to market have gone to the armouries.

ford_feud.name: The Grey Ford Feud
ford_feud.desc: Blood has been spilt on the Ford again, and the border clans have taken up spears with grim contentment.

ford_riders.name: Riders at the Ford
ford_riders.desc: The horsemen of the high glens ride down to the river like a hailstorm.

law_above_all.name: No Man Above the Law
law_above_all.desc: The Lawspeaker's rule is known in every glen: king and cattle-thief answer alike.

horse_clans_spirit.name: The Horse Clans
horse_clans_spirit.desc: The plain-clans ride in loose companies that are everywhere, and never where the enemy expects.

clan_war_bands_spirit.name: The Clan War-Bands
clan_war_bands_spirit.desc: Rival war-bands now march under one standard, and still sing their own songs.

western_host.name: The Western Host
western_host.desc: Hill-men, horse-lords and house-carls in one army, blessed on the Rock.

sea_captains.name: The Sea-Captains' Guild
sea_captains.desc: A ladder of ranks, a book of signals and a fund for widows: the sea-captains have become a brotherhood.

transports.name: Transports of the West
transports.desc: Broad cogs, fitted with horse-stalls and extra stores, wait at every quay.

crossing_fleet.name: The Crossing Fleet
crossing_fleet.desc: Hundreds of hulls under every western plaid, drilled to land a host in a day.

isle_landings.name: Landings on the Isle
isle_landings.desc: The first landing parties are on the green isle, and the sea behind them is white with sails.

beachheads.name: The Beachheads
beachheads.desc: Harbours taken and stores landed; the western army has a foothold and means to use it.

march_on_parim_spirit.name: The March on Parim
march_on_parim_spirit.desc: Every man on the road believes the road ends in the Golden City.

western_garrison.name: Governors of Parim
western_garrison.desc: Garrisons at every gate and bridge keep the city quiet, and make the hosts that hold it fewer than the city requires.

crown_across_the_sea.name: A Crown Across the Sea
crown_across_the_sea.desc: A western king sits in Parim, and the western court has gained an empire and a very long supply line.

western_trade_league_spirit.name: The Western Trade League
western_trade_league_spirit.desc: One tariff, one weight and one court for disputed cargoes across the West.

western_peace.name: The Western Peace
western_peace.desc: A peace the West made for itself, with no governor from abroad.

shields_on_the_shore_spirit.name: Shields on the Shore
shields_on_the_shore_spirit.desc: Western shield-walls hold the far coast, and every watch knows the one beside it.

wardens_beyond_the_sea_spirit.name: Wardens Beyond the Sea
wardens_beyond_the_sea_spirit.desc: The West keeps a watch on a foreign coast as a friend, and is proud of it.

old_banner.name: Under the War-King's Banner
old_banner.desc: The old banner is flown again, and the men who knew it ride a little taller.

against_the_deathless_spirit.name: Against the Deathless
against_the_deathless_spirit.desc: The companies have learned what stops the dead, and what does not.

clan_moot.title: The Clan Moot
clan_moot.desc: Every clan has come to the moor under its own plaid. The old chiefs say they are tired of burying sons; the young ones say that what is owed to the dead must be paid. The king waits for the noise to settle and asks what the clans will have.

options.name: The clans ask for their due.

datids_grievance.title: Thane Datid's Grievance
datids_grievance.desc: Thane Datid Werlen stands in the hall with a roll of names in his hand: the men killed at the Ford, the herds taken, the houses burned. His voice does not rise, and the room has gone very quiet. The king may hear him out, or tell his guards to remove him.

aenoran_gold.title: The Price of Aenoran Gold
aenoran_gold.desc: A chest of coin has come from Parim, with a letter hoping that Gunwaith will find the court's friendship useful. The thanes look at the gold and the Lawspeaker looks at the thanes. The king knows that a gift from the Golden Court is rarely a gift.

buldor_contracts.title: Contracts from Gunwaith
buldor_contracts.desc: Envoys from Gunwaith have come to the captains of Buldor with a new offer: steady pay, a share in the spoils and the king's protection if the swords go west. The captains are practical men, and the offer is practical, though a good deal less lucrative than Aenor's.

options.name: Our swords go to whoever pays most.

island_charter.title: A Charter for the Western Fleet
island_charter.desc: Gunwaith asks the island kingdoms to sell their charts, their steersmen and the use of their yards. The islanders have kept their knowledge for generations and are used to being asked for it; they are less used to being paid.

options.name: Sell the charts and the ships.
The islands keep out of it.

dead_and_south.title: Death from the North, Fire from the South
dead_and_south.desc: The scouts return grey-faced. The dead are on the northern roads and something worse is moving from the south, and the western army is between them with its back to the sea. The captains have two plans, and neither is comfortable.

options.name: Hold the line while we can.

equals_across_the_sea.title: Equals Across the Sea
equals_across_the_sea.desc: A letter has arrived from Gunwaith, sealed with the boar and the plaid. It proposes a charter between the crown of Aenor and the crown of Gunwaith, as equals, ending the long ledger of conquest and tribute. The letter is courteous and quite firm.

focuses.name: The Clan Halls of Gunwaith
focuses.desc: Gunwaith is a crown of clans, and the king rules only so far as the halls consent. King Herlic calls the great chiefs to his table to settle who sits where, who pays what and who may speak first.

focuses.name: The Truce-Maker's Court
focuses.desc: The king who signed the Truce of the Grey Ford keeps a court for those who want it to hold: reeves, ford-wardens and mothers who have lost sons. They are not loud, but there are many of them.

focuses.name: The Thanes Speak
focuses.desc: The war-thanes have been silent for three winters, and have not enjoyed it. Now they rise in the hall one after another to say what the truce has cost: stolen herds, cold hearths and a southern border that nobody trusts.

focuses.name: Call the Clan Moot
focuses.desc: Once in a generation the clans gather on the open moor, each under its own plaid, and say aloud what they want. The king must listen, whether or not he likes the answer.

focuses.name: Thane Datid's Grievance
focuses.desc: Thane Datid Werlen brings the names of the herds lifted at the Ford and demands that the king read them before the moot. The king can hear him or hush him, and either way the whole hall will watch.

focuses.name: The King's Peace
focuses.desc: The king declares a peace that will outlast him: no raid, no reprisal and no blood-price to be taken in his name. Warriors who break it answer to the Lawspeaker, however high their house.

focuses.name: Heed the War-Thanes
focuses.desc: The king gives the thanes what they ask: the right to answer insult with iron and a seat nearest the throne. The clans are tired, but they are also proud, and pride is cheaper to raise than patience.

focuses.name: One Law, One Crown
focuses.desc: Whichever voice has won the hall, the king now binds the clans to a single code under a single crown. The oldest chiefs grumble that it was not so in their grandfathers' days, and sign.

focuses.name: The Clan Levies Charter
focuses.desc: Each clan promises a fixed levy, to be mustered on the king's summons and sent home at the first frost. For the first time the number is written on a roll, and not left to the chief's mood.

focuses.name: Taryn's Banner
focuses.desc: Bards sing of Taryn of Gunwaith, who would not draw her sword for the Grand Alliance until its captains named her clan with honour. The banner she carried is carried again at every moot.

effects.tooltip: Gunwaith's banner flew in the First Age under its own commanders.

focuses.name: The Clans as One
focuses.desc: At the end of the year of feasts, the chiefs join hands over the king's cup and drink. It is a gesture, and the hall has been waiting a hundred years to see it made.

focuses.name: The Horse Fairs
focuses.desc: Twice a year the whole of the West comes to the moorland fairs to buy Gunwaith's horses. The tolls fill the king's chests, and a new hall of stalls and smithies rises beside the market ground.

focuses.name: The Highland Studs
focuses.desc: Stud-masters of the high glens breed a hardy, sure-footed pony that thrives on heather and poor grass. They are not fast, but they cross a moor in the rain and still come home.

focuses.name: Timber Rights of the Clans
focuses.desc: The clans have long quarrelled over who may cut the northern forests. The king declares a rule of shares, and a shipwright's yard rises at the river mouth to take the first of the logs.

focuses.name: The Market Towns
focuses.desc: Where the drove roads cross, the clans grant charters for walled markets. A town is a new thing in the glens, but a trader's coin does not care for custom.

focuses.name: Sawmills of the West
focuses.desc: Water-driven saws are set on the northern rivers, turning whole forests into planks. The great beams that once had to be hauled by hand now arrive sawn and stacked.

focuses.name: The Neck Road
focuses.desc: North of Gunwaith the land narrows to a neck of rock and ice, and beyond it lie the Cold Lands. A road is staked out over it, and a letter goes to Fandanar to ask whether the lords of Coldor would meet it halfway.

focuses.name: Western Forges
focuses.desc: Smiths who once worked for a single clan now share a street of forges and a master of the guild. Their spearheads are marked with the king's boar so that every buyer knows what he is getting.

focuses.name: No Tariff Without Answer
focuses.desc: Aenor's customs-men take their toll at every western port, and Parim calls it a courtesy. The king writes a letter that is polite in every line and says in the last that the West has counted what it has paid.

focuses.name: The War Chest of the West
focuses.desc: Tolls, tributes and the sale of a thousand horses are gathered in the king's vaults, with a clerk to count them and a chief to keep the keys. Whatever the West decides to do, Gunwaith will be able to pay for its share.

focuses.name: The Grey Ford
focuses.desc: The Grey Ford is a shallow crossing of a cold river, and a place where both sides once left their dead. The truce was signed on its north bank, on a table made from two doors.

focuses.name: The Ford Commission
focuses.desc: A joint commission of Gunwaith clan-lords and Girdon wardens is proposed, to settle every herd, every boundary stone and every complaint before it becomes a feud. It is less romantic than a battle, and a good deal cheaper.

focuses.name: Garrisons on the Ford
focuses.desc: The thanes demand stout walls on the north bank, and the king agrees that a wall is not a war. Girdon may disagree, and the truce will be quieter without the new stone to look at.

focuses.name: Shared Tolls at the Ford
focuses.desc: The tolls on the crossing are split by agreement, half to the king and half to the wardens of Girdon. Each side now earns by the other's traffic, and neither wishes to see it stop.

focuses.name: Answer the Ford Raids
focuses.desc: The clans on the border pay each raid back in kind: a herd for a herd and a burned barn for a burned barn. It is exactly the kind of thing that wears a truce to threads.

focuses.name: The Ford Holds
focuses.desc: After years of quiet the king and the Warden-Speaker meet on the Ford and cut the truce-stone in two, leaving each half in the water. What was a pause in the war has become a peace.

focuses.name: Blood at the Grey Ford
focuses.desc: The truce is broken, and the first dead are already carried north across the stones. The thanes call it their due; the Lawspeaker calls it the beginning of a very long list.

focuses.name: A Bridge of Stone at the Ford
focuses.desc: Masons from both banks build a bridge where the Ford was, with an oath carved on either parapet. Nobody who walks across it can claim not to know what the two kingdoms swore.

focuses.name: Ride to the Ford
focuses.desc: The riders of the high glens answer the king's horn, a hundred horsemen to a clan and none of them quiet. The Ford has been fought over before, and they know the ground better than they know their own beds.

focuses.name: Peace at the Ford
focuses.desc: The feud is over. Both sides have buried their dead and burned the blood-price rolls, and the wardens of the Ford are told again that they keep a crossing and not a battlefield.

focuses.name: Brothers of the Ford
focuses.desc: Gunwaith and Girdon clasp hands on the Bridge and call each other brothers, which is more than either expected. A pact of non-aggression is signed, and the old grudges are put down at last.

focuses.name: Girdon Must Bend
focuses.desc: The thanes insist that a rival who has been beaten once must be beaten into a lesson. The king puts his seal on a list of claims on Girdon's lands, and the western courts read it with interest.

focuses.name: The River League
focuses.desc: The two kingdoms bind themselves to defend the rivers and the sea beyond them: shared yards, shared steersmen, shared enemies. In ten years the Ford will be a thing their children read about.

focuses.name: The River Mouths
focuses.desc: Girdon's rivers run out to the sea through the mouths that Gunwaith has always wanted. With the claims drawn and the dark gathering, the king decides that now is the time to take them.

focuses.name: The Lawspeaker's Rock
focuses.desc: On a grey rock at the centre of Gunwaith the Lawspeaker recites the law at every new moon, from memory, without a book. Kings have stood before it to be corrected, and been corrected.

focuses.name: The Old Law Rolls
focuses.desc: Lawspeaker Ilurda has the old customs written down at last, so that a young judge need not be an old woman to know them. The rolls are kept in a stone chest, and she keeps the key.

focuses.name: Judges on Circuit
focuses.desc: Judges ride from glen to glen with the law in their heads and a pony apiece, settling feuds before they begin. The clans fear them more than they fear the king, and are the better for it.

focuses.name: No Man Above the Law
focuses.desc: The Lawspeaker declares it at the Rock for all to hear: no chief, no thane and no king is above the law of Gunwaith, and any traveller who enters the kingdom is bound by it. The words are carved on the stone.

focuses.name: A Judgment Remembered
focuses.desc: A stranger once stood before the Rock and asked to be judged as any man of the clans, and was. The Lawspeaker remembers what he said, and the clans remember that he did not ask to be spared.

focuses.name: The War-King Remembered
focuses.desc: For one season the confederation of the West made that stranger its war-king, and he laid the title down when the work was done. The thanes tell it as a boast, and the Lawspeaker as a lesson.

focuses.name: Songs of the King Without a House
focuses.desc: Bards compose songs about the king without a house, who rode the moors and made peace between rivals and then rode away. The songs grow longer with each telling, and the king in them grows less like the man.

focuses.name: Weigh the Warning from the East
focuses.desc: A warning has reached the Rock from the man the West once crowned and then forgot. The Lawspeaker asks the clans to weigh it as they would weigh any testimony, and not to dismiss it because of who is speaking.

focuses.name: The Clans in Arms
focuses.desc: The clans have always fought, but never together. The king calls the war-bands to the moor and puts them through a month of drill under officers who are neither their uncles nor their rivals.

focuses.name: Hill-Warriors of the North
focuses.desc: The men of the high glens fight with hill-spears and rounded shields, climbing faster than the lowlanders can follow. They learn the new drill the way they learn everything: by doing it a hundred times.

focuses.name: The Horse Clans
focuses.desc: The clans of the western plain are born in the saddle, and their hosts are the swiftest in the West. They ride in loose companies, and the king agrees to leave them that way.

focuses.name: Drill on the Moors
focuses.desc: Captains who served abroad teach the clans to march in step, to keep a line and to hold it when the man beside them falls. The moors echo with horns, and the sheep complain.

focuses.name: Lancers of Gunwaith
focuses.desc: A company of heavy horsemen is raised from the sons of the great houses, with lance, mail and a war-horse bred for the charge. They are costly, and they know it.

focuses.name: The Clan War-Bands
focuses.desc: The war-bands of the clans, once rivals, now have a common standard and a common word of command. They still sing their own songs on the march, but they sing them in the same key.

focuses.name: The Hill Forts
focuses.desc: Old hill-forts are repaired and linked by signal fires, so that a raid on one clan brings help from three. The thanes say the forts are to keep out Girdon, and the king chooses not to ask.

focuses.name: Muster of the Thanes
focuses.desc: Every thane who holds land of the king answers the call with his full strength: housecarls, tenants, cousins and the dogs. It is the largest host Gunwaith has put together since the First Age.

focuses.name: The Western Host
focuses.desc: The clans, the horse-lords and the hill-men are formed into one army with one banner, and the Lawspeaker blesses it on the Rock. It is the host that the West will send, if the West sends anyone.

focuses.name: Voices of the West
focuses.desc: Envoys ride to every court of the West, carrying the king's greeting and a pointed question: how much has Aenor taken from you this year? The answers are longer than anyone expected.

focuses.name: Envoys to the Western Courts
focuses.desc: Resident envoys are sent to the larger courts, with letters of credit and orders to listen at table. A man who dines with a king hears what the king would not say in council.

focuses.name: The Price of Aenoran Gold
focuses.desc: Parim's gold has found its way into the pockets of western lords, with its usual gentle conditions. The king must decide whether to take his share or tell the court in Parim what he thinks of its generosity.

focuses.name: The Merchant Free Towns
focuses.desc: The trading towns of the south-west have no kings, only counting-houses, and they are the angriest of all about Aenor's tariffs. Gunwaith offers them its horses, its timber and its ear.

focuses.name: The Old Crowns of the West
focuses.desc: The ancient crowns of the West hold that they were kings before Aenor was an army. They remember being ruled from Parim, and are quick to say so over wine.

focuses.name: The Buldor Contracts
focuses.desc: The sell-sword companies of Buldor take pay from any court that offers it, and Aenor has been one of their best customers. Gunwaith offers a different contract and a better purse.

focuses.name: Convene the Ford Council
focuses.desc: The kings and captains of the West are summoned to the Ford, where the truce was signed, to sit at one table. For once, the table has been laid for something other than the dead.

focuses.name: The Western Purse
focuses.desc: The courts of the West pool a purse for common works: harbour chains, ships for the common good and pay for the Buldor captains. Whoever holds the purse will be asked what it is for.

focuses.name: The Grievances of the West
focuses.desc: The council puts on parchment every wrong that Aenor has done the West: the conquests, the tariffs, the banners at Dardan that Parim forgot to praise. It is a very long list, and it is read aloud.

focuses.name: A God on Aenor's Throne
focuses.desc: Parim's new king is worshipped as a deliverer, and the western courts are not sure whether that is a promise or a warning. The council agrees only that a god who is crowned as king answers to no one in the West.

focuses.name: The Question of the Sea
focuses.desc: The council unrolls the western charts and puts a finger on the central sea. Across it lies the Middle Lands, and the oldest claims of the West; nobody at the table can say for sure what the sea will cost.

focuses.name: Cross for the Old Claims
focuses.desc: The western kings agree that the old claims will be pressed on the far shore, with fleets and hosts. It is the greatest decision in a thousand years, and it was taken in an afternoon.

focuses.name: The West Keeps Its Own Shore
focuses.desc: The courts decide that no sea is worth crossing for an old grudge, and the West will be the master of its own coast and its own market. A quiet decision, and the harder for it.

focuses.name: The Western Relief
focuses.desc: Word has reached the Ford that the dark is stirring in the Middle Lands. The West will not cross to conquer; it will cross to stand beside the people whose claims it once pressed.

focuses.name: Western Shipwrights
focuses.desc: Shipwrights from the river towns are given royal charters and the best of the northern oak. They have built coasting boats for centuries; the king asks them what it would take to build something bigger.

focuses.name: Merchant Fleets of the West
focuses.desc: A hundred merchant cogs sail under Gunwaith's plaid, carrying wool, horses and timber to the ports of three coasts. The ships are slow and broad, and they pay for themselves in two seasons.

focuses.name: Harbours of Gunwaith
focuses.desc: Stone quays, deep moorings and warehouse halls are built along the northern coast. A harbour that can shelter a hundred ships can shelter a hundred and one.

focuses.name: Charts of the Pupor Ocean
focuses.desc: The island kingdoms of the Pupor Ocean know the currents and the stars as the clans know their glens. Gunwaith offers a fair price for their charts, and a better one for their steersmen.

focuses.name: Timber from the North
focuses.desc: The great oaks of the northern forests are felled in winter, floated down the rivers in spring and seasoned in the yards for years. A keel laid today will be sound for a generation.

focuses.name: War Galleys
focuses.desc: Long, low galleys with a ram at the prow and a hundred oars to the side are laid down in the northern yards. They are not made for the open ocean, but they will carry a host across a strait.

focuses.name: The Sea-Captains' Guild
focuses.desc: Masters of the great ships are chartered into a guild with a ladder of ranks, a common book of signals and a fund for widows. The best of them have crossed the wide ocean; most, until now, never had a reason.

focuses.name: The Great Yards
focuses.desc: Where there were three slips there are now twelve, under a roof a hundred paces long. The noise of caulking can be heard from the hills.

focuses.name: Ships for a Long Voyage
focuses.desc: The council agrees that if the West is to sail, it must sail in strength. Every yard gets its quota of hulls and every captain his assigned station; the shipwrights are told there will be no excuses.

focuses.name: Transports of the West
focuses.desc: Broad-bellied cogs are fitted with horse-stalls and extra stores, crews are trained to load a host in a day and a half, and a steersman is assigned to every hull. Every one of them is meant to be filled.

focuses.name: Escorts for the Host
focuses.desc: War galleys and great warships are drilled to sail in line around the transports, answering to one flag. The rule is simple and the captains learn it quickly: no ship is left behind.

focuses.name: The Crossing Fleet
focuses.desc: Hundreds of hulls are gathered in the northern harbours under the plaids of every western court. When they weigh anchor, it is said, the whole coast hears the horns.

focuses.name: The Call to Cross
focuses.desc: Heralds ride to every court of the West with the king's summons: the old claims will be pressed, and every banner is asked to say how many men, how many ships and how soon. The answers will decide how large the West's ambition can be.

focuses.name: Oaths on the Shore
focuses.desc: On the northern strand each king and chief takes the oath of the crossing, with a handful of salt water at his lips. The oath binds them to sail together and to land together, and it forgives no one who breaks it.

focuses.name: The Sea-Lords' Plan
focuses.desc: Admiral Ostra Velk unrolls her chart before the kings and explains, without a trace of drama, what will be needed to land a host of this size on a hostile shore. Most of the kings leave the tent thoughtful.

focuses.name: Launch the Crossing
focuses.desc: The signal fires run down the coast and the fleets weigh anchor together, a forest of masts on the morning tide. The West has not sailed like this since the old kings went north.

focuses.name: The Isle First
focuses.desc: The first sails sight the long green isle off the coast of the Middle Lands. The landing parties go ashore at dawn, and the sea behind them is white with sails.

focuses.name: The Wide Sea Crossed
focuses.desc: The central sea was wider than any chart had shown, and the fleet crossed it in storm and calm alike. Sailors who thought they had known the ocean write that they had not.

focuses.name: Seize the Western Ports
focuses.desc: The harbours on the western shore of the Middle Lands fall one by one, their garrisons surprised by the size of the fleet. Behind the quays the host unloads, and for the first time in a thousand years a western banner flies in the east.

focuses.name: The March on Parim
focuses.desc: The host leaves the coast and turns toward the Great Lake, with the king's banner at its head. Whatever the road costs, every man on it believes the road ends in Parim.

focuses.name: Accept the Surrenders
focuses.desc: Aenor's garrisons are offered terms: keep your lives, your lands and your honour, and yield your swords. Many accept, and the conquest becomes easier and quieter than anyone had planned.

focuses.name: The Keys of Parim
focuses.desc: The gates of the Golden Court open, and a delegation brings the great keys on a cushion. The captains of the West look at the keys and at one another, and nobody is sure what comes next.

focuses.name: Claim the Throne of Men
focuses.desc: The western claimant takes the old throne of men in the name of the West, and the councillors are summoned to kneel. The throne is high, and the crown, which the western claimant had thought lighter, is heavier than it looked.

focuses.name: Hold Parim as a Pledge
focuses.desc: The captains agree that the city is held as a pledge for the redress of the West's grievances, and that the throne is left empty until terms are signed. It is a cautious choice and a very expensive one.

focuses.name: Governors of Parim
focuses.desc: Governors are named for the captured districts, and garrisons are posted at every bridge and gate. The people of the city look at them with polite hatred, and wait.

focuses.name: Death from the North, Fire from the South
focuses.desc: Reports come in from two directions at once: the dead are marching out of the north, and a darker host is moving up from the south. The West has crossed the sea to take a throne and found itself standing in the way of both.

focuses.name: Sail Home
focuses.desc: The order is given at dawn: the army will go home. The garrisons are called in, the horses are led down to the quays and the banners are folded one by one.

focuses.name: Hold What We Took
focuses.desc: The captains refuse to sail. They have bled for these stones, they say, and the dead of the West will not have died for a sea-passage home.

focuses.name: The Fleet at the Shore
focuses.desc: Every ship that can float is sent back across the sea, empty, to carry the host. The sailors work without sleep, because the dead are coming, and the shore will not wait.

focuses.name: A Crown Across the Sea
focuses.desc: The western claimant is crowned in Parim with the old crown of men, and the West suddenly has a king on the far shore. How long he can keep the crown is a question that nobody dares to ask aloud.

focuses.name: Those Left Behind
focuses.desc: Not every soldier made it to the ships. Companies that were cut off, wounded men and a few who simply could not leave are still on the far shore, and their families at home are asking the king what he will do for them.

focuses.name: The Western Regency of Parim
focuses.desc: The new king is advised by a regency council of westerners and the better sort of Aenorans, who disagree on most things. The regency keeps the peace, and little else.

focuses.name: Our Own Shore
focuses.desc: The kings of the West agree to keep what they have and to build on it. The harbours are filled with merchant ships, the fields are tilled to the border and no fleet leaves the shore.

focuses.name: First Crown of the West
focuses.desc: Gunwaith, the strongest of the western crowns, takes the title of first among its neighbours and proclaims claims on the lands of the smallest. It is a gentle conquest, as conquests go, but a conquest all the same.

focuses.name: An Accord on the Neck
focuses.desc: A treaty is signed with the lords of Coldor over the neck of rock and ice that joins their lands to Gunwaith's. Neither side will cross it with an army, and both will use it for trade.

focuses.name: The Lesser Crowns Bend
focuses.desc: The smallest of the western kings are offered a choice between submission and the sword. Most bow, and the first neighbour who does not will find the claims already drawn.

focuses.name: The Western Trade League
focuses.desc: The courts of the West agree on a single tariff, a single standard of weight and one court for disputed cargoes. Merchants who once paid six tolls on a road now pay one.

focuses.name: The Western Peace
focuses.desc: At last the West has made a peace that it governs itself, with no governor from Parim and no army from abroad. It will be remembered as the quietest settlement of an age.

focuses.name: Letters to Parim
focuses.desc: The king writes to the Aenor realm that holds Parim: the West wishes to land as a friend, with its ships and its host, and begs a harbour on the western shore. Whether the letter is believed is a matter for Parim.

focuses.name: Answer the Lost Cause
focuses.desc: The Lost Cause, Aenor's league of the loyal, asks the West what its banners are for. Gunwaith answers by sending its own, and takes the oath of a companion.

focuses.name: The Relief Fleet
focuses.desc: Hulls that were laid down for a war are fitted for a rescue: hospital ships, grain-boats and extra cargo-lighters. The captains do not complain.

focuses.name: Land as Friends
focuses.desc: The fleet comes to the friendly quays under a white flag and the plaids of the West. Aenor's people line the harbour, unsure whether to cheer or to be afraid.

focuses.name: Shields on the Shore
focuses.desc: The western host takes post along the coast, where the dead and the dark are expected to come, and digs in. There are no heroics, only shields, spears and men who know how to hold.

focuses.name: The West Remembers Dardan
focuses.desc: Western bards sing again of the Grand Alliance, in which the clans of the West marched with the men of Aenor against the Dark King. Those who have heard the song as children are the first to volunteer.

effects.tooltip: Western banners stood with the Grand Alliance in the First Age.

focuses.name: Wardens Beyond the Sea
focuses.desc: The West takes up a long watch on the far shore as friends of the realm, with its own banners and its own captains. Nobody is under any illusion that it is a small thing to ask of a distant crown.

focuses.name: Beside Former Foes
focuses.desc: The king the West once crowned has returned, and he asks the western companies to stand beside the men they were sent to conquer. They are not subjects and he does not ask them to be; he asks them to fight.

focuses.name: Under the War-King's Banner
focuses.desc: The old war-king's banner is unfurled, and the western companies who served under it in the Ford campaigns raise a cheer. They remember that he laid down his crown without being asked.

focuses.name: Against the Deathless
focuses.desc: The dead do not tire and cannot be killed by common weapons; the westerners learn this by losing men. The remedies they find are expensive, strange and, so far, effective.

focuses.name: Hailed by the Living
focuses.desc: The roads are lined with the grateful, and the westerners are hailed as the first friends from across the sea. They had come to take, and are being thanked for having stayed.

focuses.name: The Long Way Home
focuses.desc: The war is over and the ships are brought back to the quays. The companies that stayed to the end sail with the tide, bearing honours they did not expect and scars they did not choose.

focuses.name: Equals Across the Sea
focuses.desc: The crown of Aenor and the crown of Gunwaith are asked to sign a charter as equals, with neither bowing to the other. The West has waited a thousand years for the offer, and finds that it is still hard to accept.
